title: How Can Driving World Models Do Counterfactual Prediction?

output_modality.value: Single-view driving video from frozen existing world models (Vista, DrivingWorld); benchmark videos rendered in CARLA.

control_signal.value: Alternative ego action given as a target trajectory; in the proposed pipeline also factual-continuation evidence from the recorded episode.

control_mechanism.value: Training-free: transport factual-continuation pixels into the counterfactual camera view, let the frozen world model complete unsupported regions, then a Combine stage restores the evidence. Weights unchanged.

base_model.value: Frozen Vista (diffusion-based) and DrivingWorld (autoregressive video GPT); monocular depth used for transport; DINOv2 and CLIP encoders for scoring.

datasets.value: Self-built CARLA benchmark with factual logs and matched counterfactual ground truth; scenarios include side street, lead cuts in, lead brake.

metrics.value: Recovered fractions RecD (DINOv2) and RecC (CLIP), and LPIPS against the matched counterfactual ground truth.

controllability_evidence.value: Overall on Vista RecD/RecC rise from 0.38/0.33 (direct) to 0.70/0.65, LPIPS 0.423 to 0.169; on DrivingWorld 0.31/0.24 to 0.67/0.64, LPIPS 0.291 to 0.211.

closed_loop.value: No. Open-loop, short-horizon with scripted surrounding agents; closed-loop suites with reactive agents are future work.

stated_limitations.value: Scripted agents and short horizon; models evaluated outside training render domain; depth error causes seams; method needs the factual continuation, so only retrospective queries.

notes: Analysis and benchmark paper rather than a new controllable world model; the control input studied is ego action on existing models. Table 1 column pairing read as direct vs ours per metric.
